hypothesis: At N=128 (data_seed 0, fresh seeds 24-26, otherwise identical to the paired N=64 and N=256 arms), trained force R2 itself falls relative to N=64, as it did on data_seed 1 (0.74 to 0.66 with flat controls). So the N=64-to-N=128 force decline is a decodability drop and not a control effect. Values are read from run records (unrounded) and paired per seed with the N=64 seeds 24-26 arm; if that arm is unavailable, the comparison is reported as not computed.
expected_if_true: In >= 2 of 3 seeds: trained force R2(N=128) is >= 0.04 below the same seed's N=64 value, and |force control R2(N=128) - force control R2(N=64)| <= 0.03. Final force margin in [0.06, 0.20]. Normalised accel_step in [0.60, 0.78].
expected_if_false: In >= 2 of 3 seeds, trained force R2 at N=128 is within 0.02 of N=64, or the margin drop is mostly (>50%) accounted for by a control rise. Anything else is inconclusive.
